full_judgment: 3. In the case of Ayna Dasi vs. Arena Bala Dashi and others reported in 12 D.L.R 603 it was held that "according to the established principle, in case of a document executed by an illiterate pardanashin lady, the burden lies on those who seek to bold the lady to the terms of her deed to satisfy the Court on evidence. that the deed was actually executed by her with full understanding of what she was about to do; that she had full knowledge of the nature and effect of the transaction into which she is said to have entered; and that she had independent and disinterested advice in the matter". The ease of Ayan Dasi came under review of the Appellate Division in the case of Siddique Ahmed Chowahury and others Vs. Gold Ahmed and others reported 33 DLR (AD) 1. The Appellate Division on a review of the case in the light of a number of Privy Council decisions, namely, Nawab Sekander Begum Vs. Zulfikar Wali Khan AIR 1938 (P.C) 38, Faridunnesa Vs. Mukhtar Ahmed 30 CWN 337; Sunitibala Devi Vs. Dhara Sundari Debi AIR 1919 (P.C) 21; Lala Kundan Lal Vs. Mr. Mosharrafi Begum AIR 1936 P.C (207); Ramanamma Vs. Kumawat Vs. Kunwar Digijai Singh 26 CWN 490 (P.C); and Bank of Khulna vs. Joti Prokash Mira 45 CWN 257; and also after considering some other decisions, namely, Wajid Ali Khan, 39 IA 156; Jacoor Deen Jewari vs. Nawab Syed Ali Hossan Ali Begunia, AIR 1928 P.C 303; Hemchandra Roy Chowdhury vs. Suradhari Debya Chowdhurani, AIR 1940 PC 134; Khurbuja Khir vs. Jang Bahadur AIR 1963 SC 1203 has observed that if in a of transfer by a pardanashin lady a dispute arises as to its validity, the onus is always on the party who seeks to hold the transferor to the terms of the deed to satisfy the Court on evidence that she substantially understood the disposition and she executed the deed with full understanding of what she was doing and of the nature and effect of the transaction', but independent advice by itself is not an essential burden to be discharged, unless there are some special circumstances calling for its application, in that the done or the transferee stood in a position of active confidence or had fiduciary relationship with the pardanashin lady, and it is only in such cases, the donee or transferee wilt carry the additional burden to prove that the lady had independent and disinterested advice from persons other than the recipient of the document.
